comparisons.aos-2024-v52-i05-p2004/D1: Use Matrix.submatrix with the identity row map and the increasing column inclusion omitting the final column. Fin.succAbove at the last index gives that inclusion once the original column count is represented as a successor. The resulting p-by-(n-1) matrix preserves every retained entry and its order; it neither zeros the final column nor changes the row dimension. The pair is arbitrary real matrices and carries no mixture model, randomness or independence assumption. The construction presumes a removable column rather than using natural subtraction to invent a deletion from an empty matrix.
comparisons.aos-2024-v52-i05-p2004/D6: Use the same submatrix construction with Fin.succAbove at the selected column i, keeping all other columns in their original order. This deletes one observation column from the given mixture data matrix and preserves its signal/noise decomposition by restriction. It does not refit or change the true assignments, centers or noise law, and it does not make the full and leave-one-out matrices independent. The construction retains the data-model dependency that is absent from the arbitrary-matrix D1 passage.

comparisons.aos-2024-v52-i01-p0364/D7: For the loading matrix, the source G_k stores descending eigenvalues of A_k^T*A_k, hence squared singular values of A_k; its square root is the diagonal singular-value factor. A right Gram eigenbasis and square roots provide the components, and for positive singular values the paired left vectors are A*v/sigma. Rank-deficient cases need orthonormal completion instead of dividing by zero, while this loading context supplies its own full-column-rank conditions. Keep Q_k=A_k*D_k^(-1/2) separate: equality of its column span with A_k requires invertibility of the diagonal normalization, and its normalized-Gram limit is a model assumption, not an SVD consequence. Eigenvectors are only specified up to signs and rotations under repeated eigenvalues.
comparisons.aos-2024-v52-i05-p2004/D2: Preserve the two rectangular decompositions as sums of singular-value-weighted outer products, with lengths min(p,n-1) and min(p,n), and the corresponding leading-r left frames. The spectral primitives supply ordered values and Gram eigenbases, but the paired left/right vectors and exact reconstruction must be assembled, including zero-singular-value completions when needed. The library values are zero-indexed and padded by zeros; the source's finite sequence does not automatically adopt that extension for sigma_(r+1) at its last allowed r. Keep that endpoint issue and unspecified measurable/tie selection. The two matrices differ by a column, but their chosen bases need not be aligned or have matching signs.

comparisons.aos-2024-v52-i05-p2004/D7: For each of the full and leave-one-column-out observed matrices, use an eigenbasis of its left Gram operator and select the requested leading directions in descending singular-value order. These are empirical data subspaces, not singular vectors of the rank-at-most-k signal matrix P. The permission r in [k] does not alone prove r is within both finite SVD lengths; preserve the saved dimension/endpoint limitation rather than silently padding the frame with extra vectors. Zero-padding scalar singular values does not supply such vectors. Signs, repeated-eigenvalue rotations and measurable selection remain unspecified, and a truncation through a tied singular value need not define a unique subspace.
comparisons.aos-2024-v52-i06-p2641/D11: The LSVD_m output can be built from the first m columns of a descending left-Gram eigenbasis for its supplied input matrix. It requires an admissible truncation dimension and an orthonormal output frame; it is not the list of scalar singular values. A chosen eigenbasis is not unique under ties, and a spectral tie at the cutoff can change the selected subspace. The noncomputable existence of an eigenbasis does not establish a measurable algorithmic selection for the paper's random matrix input. Keep the original operator and its input choices, without adding signal-rank or eigengap conditions from later sufficient assumptions.

comparison: Retain the literal distinctness statement for the singular values of G_k. In the surrounding decomposition G_k is a nonnegative diagonal matrix of eigenvalues of A_k^T*A_k, so its diagonal entries are squared singular values of A_k, not the singular values of A_k themselves. Positivity makes the relevant distinctness equivalent after taking square roots, but that is an elementary consequence to prove, not a change to the quoted object. Apply pairwise inequality only over the source's finite list; the library's infinite zero padding would make distinctness over all natural indices impossible. Distinctness gives no uniform eigengap size. Preserve its restricted use for eigenvector-alignment clauses in Theorems 1,2,4 and the recorded all-assumption imports in 6,7,9.

comparison: For each subject use the function-valued model mu_i plus delta_i times the strict event t>tau_i plus the error. The change therefore starts after tau_i, not at it; subjects may have different mean functions, jumps and break locations, and a zero jump represents no effective break. Temporal stationarity is a separate property of each error process, not independence across time or subjects. Under distributional stationarity it can be expressed by IdentDistrib of every finite time block and its admissible shift, not merely equality of one-time marginals; do not replace it by i.i.d. errors. If only a weaker moment-stationarity convention is intended, that must remain a separate interpretation rather than silently strengthening the source. The standing function-space quotient and moment qualifications remain applicable, and no common break or cross-subject independence is introduced.
gap: Indicators and equal-law predicates provide model components; the intended stationarity convention and function-space interpretation must be specified separately.
